neighbours.label: a narrative beat after dialogue where one character reads another's face or reaction
fire: "You knew," I said. He searched my face for a moment, then looked away.
"It's nothing," she whispered. Fear flickered across her face before she hid it.
"Are you sure?" Tom asked. He studied her expression, trying to read it.
"Fine," he muttered. She could tell from his face that he was furious.
"I'll be back soon," Mara promised. Her brother scanned her face, unconvinced.
"Who told you?" Shame flashed across his face, and he lowered his eyes.
"Thank you," she said. He watched her face soften as she read the letter.
"Don't worry," Dad said. I studied his face for any sign that he was lying.
quiet: "You knew," I said. Then I picked up my coat and walked to the door.
"It's nothing," she whispered, and she put the kettle on the stove.
"Are you sure?" Tom asked, while he loaded the dishwasher.
"Fine," he muttered, and he drove the rest of the way in silence.
"I'll be back soon," Mara promised, and she closed the gate behind her.
The museum opens at ten and closes at six, except on public holidays.
"Thank you," she said, and she put the letter in her bag.
"Don't worry," Dad said, and he went outside to fix the car.
